q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after market close. Today is August 25, 2026. **Resolution occurs in approximately 24 hours.**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (not actual Q2 FY2027 results). This means the guidance NVIDIA will issue on August 26 for its Q3 FY2027 quarter.

Key facts from the research:
- NVIDIA's May guidance for Q2 FY2027 was $91.0B ± 2% ($89.2B–$92.8B)
- Wall Street consensus is $91.8B–$91.9B
- The sequential Q2 add of $9.4B is smaller than the previous three quarters (suggesting potential moderation in growth)
- This guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue

The most likely scenario is that NVIDIA provides conservative but achievable forward guidance. NVIDIA typically guides to ranges they can reliably beat or meet, and has shown discipline in managing expectations. The slowdown in sequential revenue growth ($9.4B vs prior three quarters) suggests the company may be cautious about aggressive projections.

Given that:
- The guidance range provided ($99.5B–$115.5B) is centered around $107.5B
- The previous quarter's guidance was $91.0B
- Sequential growth of ~$9.4B would imply $100.4B for Q3
- But NVIDIA often guides for modest acceleration in the quarter after earnings

**Most likely outcome: $105B–$109B range** – representing modest sequential growth and reflecting continued AI demand without extraordinary upside assumptions.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Deteriorating AI capex cycle**: If NVIDIA sees signs of demand saturation or customer inventory buildup
- **Macro weakness**: Recession signals or customer credit concerns would reduce capital spending
- **China restrictions intensifying**: Though already excluded, further restrictions might dampen overall sentiment
- **Competitive pressure**: AMD or other competitors gaining market share faster than expected
- **Inventory corrections**: If customers are destocking, demand could soften

This might result in guidance in the $99.5B–$103B range.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-expected data center orders**: New AI model deployments or hyperscaler infrastructure builds accelerating
- **China revenue surprise**: Positive developments allowing China Data Center revenue inclusion
- **AI adoption accelerating**: Broader enterprise adoption beyond hyperscalers
- **Higher ASP**: If customers purchase higher-margin H200 or next-gen products
- **Capacity constraints**: If supply constraints limit revenue but create confidence in demand strength

This might result in guidance exceeding $110B, potentially reaching $112B–$115B.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Q2 FY2027 guidance was $91.0B** (issued in May for August quarter)
- The sequential add of $9.4B is explicitly stated as **smaller than the previous three quarters**
- This suggests deceleration in sequential growth rate

No other historical base rates or named precedents appear in the provided research for forward guidance patterns.

---

## Reasoning on the range estimate

The forecast range ($99.5B–$115.5B) is quite wide, centered at $107.5B. This represents roughly 18% sequential growth from the $91.0B Q2 guidance midpoint. Historical sequential growth patterns suggest this is reasonable but on the optimistic side given the explicit callout that recent sequential growth has been decelerating.

NVIDIA typically provides achievable guidance with modest conservative bias. Given:
- Deceleration signals in the research
- The wide external analyst range ($91.8B–$93B consensus for Q2 actual)
- Typical management conservatism
- But sustained AI demand strength

I estimate the forward guidance will land in the **$104B–$109B range**, with the mode around $106B–$107B.

---

NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after market close, with an analyst call at 2 p.m. PT [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026), [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8). The company's own guidance, issued in May, projects Q2 FY2027 revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, implying a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

Wall Street analysts, compiled by Yahoo! Finance, have an average revenue estimate of $91.9 billion, with Zacks Consensus Estimate at $91.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). This means the company needs to land in the upper half of its own guided range to meet the consensus [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). Citi analysts, however, expect revenue of $93 billion, about $1 billion above the Wall Street consensus [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-rethinks-nvidia-stock-ahead-163300755.html). The guided sequential revenue add of $9.4 billion is smaller than the previous three quarters [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026).
